description:
## Question

Elixir mode is normative (see "Should a kernel body also run as plain Elixir?"): every C/Elixir disagreement is a bug unless it is a listed divergence. How is agreement checked: which input generators (edge values such as i64 overflow boundaries, empty and length-1 arrays, out-of-bounds indices, division by zero, extreme floats), which tests run in both modes (catalog kernels, the subset's own tests, every docs/language.md example), how errors are compared (same exception type and message?), and what the check costs in CI time.

comments.text: Per 'What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?' (defk-dtw.7): the generators must deliberately cover out-of-range array writes, i64 overflow boundaries, inf/NaN-producing operations and aliasing patterns; these tests replace a manual audit of differences.

title: How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?
